([[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]) | college = | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = Team OTE | years2 = 2022–present | team2 = City Reapers | highlights = * [[Overtime Elite|OTE]] champion (2023) * All-OTE First Team (2023) }} '''Amen Thompson'''{{cite web |title=Amen Thompson |url=https://overtimeelite.com/players/e763b02b-3045-4a91-a078-7140899327d0 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=January 27, 2023}} (born January 30, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the City Reapers of [[Overtime Elite]] (OTE). He played basketball for [[Pine Crest School]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]], where he was rated a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and won a state title. Thompson bypassed his senior year of high school to sign with OTE, where he played for two seasons and helped his team win the league title while earning All-OTE First Team honors in 2023. ==Early life== Thompson was born to Maya Wilson and Troy Thompson and raised in [[San Leandro, California]].{{cite web |last1=Gutierrez |first1=Israel |title=The Thompson twins and Overtime Elite's unproven path to the NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34487913/the-thompson-twins-elite-unproven-path-nba |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=August 31, 2022}}{{cite web |last1=Polacheck |first1=Jacob |title=An Audacious Dream Meets Itself in Reality: A Look Inside Overtime Elite's Inaugural Season |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2022/04/18/an-audacious-dream-meets-itself-in-reality-a-look-inside-overtime-elites-inaugural-season/ |publisher=Zagsblog |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=April 18, 2022}} His identical twin brother, [[Ausar Thompson|Ausar]], is an NBA prospect, and his older brother, Troy Jr., played [[college basketball]] for [[Prairie View A&M Panthers basketball|Prairie View A&M]]. His uncle, [[Mark Thompson (hurdler)|Mark Thompson]], represented [[Jamaica]] in [[Athletics at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Men's 400 metres hurdles|400 meter hurdles]] at the [[1992 Summer Olympics]]. He and Ausar began training for basketball under the guidance of their father by age seven and drew inspiration from [[LeBron James]]. The twins were [[Homeschooling|homeschooled]] in sixth and seventh grade to focus on basketball. ==High school career== Entering eighth grade, Thompson and his family moved to [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]] so that he and Ausar could play high school basketball one year early at [[Pine Crest School]].{{cite web |last1=Schoenfield |first1=Bruce |title=The Teenagers Getting Six Figures to Leave Their High Schools for Basketball |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/30/magazine/overtime-elite-basketball-nba.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=November 30, 2021}} The twins immediately started for the team.{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=David |title='I did not think we were going to win': Pine Crest wins state title with miracle comeback |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/high-school/prep-broward/article249715043.html |website=[[Miami Herald]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=March 6, 2021}} As a sophomore at Pine Crest, Thompson averaged 16.9 points, 7.3 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game, earning All-[[Broward County, Florida|County]] honorable mention. Entering his junior season, he was named to the Broward County Fab Five by the ''[[Sun-Sentinel]]''.{{cite web |last1=Lichtenstein |first1=Adam |title=Broward County boys basketball Fab Five for 2020 (and the next five) |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball-boys/fl-sp-hs-boys-fab-five-broward-2020-20201215-xchw56365nft5kj73jym3z7uw4-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=December 15, 2020}} He averaged 20.5 points, 8.4 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game as a junior, leading his team to the Class 4A state championship in a 90–83 double [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] win over [[Santa Fe High School (Florida)|Santa Fe High School]].{{cite web |last1=Lichtenstein |first1=Adam |title=Broward 5A-1A boys basketball co-players of the year: Ausar Thompson and Amen Thompson, Pine Crest juniors |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/all-county/fl-sp-ss-prem-ac-br-bhoop-small-poy-20210328-qjyzjbndyndqpksczpjufut46q-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=March 27, 2021}} In the title game, Thompson scored 43 points and helped Pine Crest overcome an eight-point deficit with 45 seconds left in overtime. He shared Broward County Class 5A-1A co-player of the year honors from the ''Sun-Sentinel'' with Ausar. ===Recruiting=== Thompson was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{cite web |title=Amen Thompson - Basketball Recruiting |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/243378/amen-thompson |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 27, 2023}}{{cite web |title=Amen Thompson, 2022 Point Guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/amen-thompson-260426?view=pv |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 27, 2023}} He gained interest from college programs in 2019, receiving a scholarship offer from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Justin |title=South Florida's Thompson Twins are catching on with recruiters |url=https://hoopseen.com/news/player/201910/south-floridas-thompson-twins-are-catching-recruiters |publisher=HoopSeen |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=October 2, 2019}} After his junior year, Thompson held offers from Alabama, Arizona, Auburn, Arizona State and Kansas, among other programs, before deciding to not play [[college basketball]].{{cite web |last1=Brnaham |first1=Travis |title=Elite twins Amen and Ausar Thompson skip college to join the Overtime Elite program career== === Team OTE (2021–2022) === On May 25, 2021, Thompson signed a two-year contract with [[Overtime Elite]] (OTE), a new professional league based in [[Atlanta]] with players between ages 16 and 20. He joined the league with Ausar, bypassing his final year of high school and college, because he felt that it would prepare him best for the NBA.{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Overtime Elite lands another set of twins as Amen and Ausar Thompson choose professional program over college |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/overtime-elite-lands-another-set-of-twins-as-amen-and-ausar-thompson-choose-professional-program-over-college/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=May 25, 2021}}{{cite magazine |last1=Woo |first1=Jeremy |title=Can Overtime Elite Disrupt Basketball With ... Twins? |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/03/07/overtime-elite-thompson-twins-daily-cover |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=March 7, 2022}} In the 2021–22 season, Thompson played for Team OTE, one of three teams in the league, and averaged 14 points, 6.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 2.1 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Araiza |first1=Robert |title=Amen & Ausar Thompson: Should the San Antonio Spurs roll the dice? |url=https://airalamo.com/posts/amen-ausar-thompson-should-san-antonio-spurs-roll-dice/2 |publisher=Air Alamo |agency=[[FanSided]]|access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=January 13, 2023}}{{cite web |last1=Sprung |first1=Shlomo |title=Overtime Elite Roster 2022-23 |url=https://boardroom.tv/overtime-elite-roster-2022-23/ |publisher=Boardroom |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=August 26, 2022}} He competed against other OTE teams, as well as [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] and [[Postgraduate year|postgraduate]] opponents.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Overtime Elite announces 2021-22 schedule, roster for inaugural season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32381206/over-elite-announces-2021-22-schedule-roster-inaugural-season |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=October 13, 2021}} He helped his team achieve a runner-up finish, scoring 13 points in a 52–45 loss to Team Elite in the decisive third game of the finals.{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=Team Elite Wins First Overtime Elite Championship |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/b82a7362-6679-4e97-be6a-bf55e3294708 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=March 14, 2022}} Thompson played for OTE affiliate Team Overtime in [[The Basketball Tournament 2022|The Basketball Tournament]] in July 2022. His team lost to Omaha Blue Crew, 74–70, in the first round of the tournament.{{cite web |last1=DeMarinis |first1=Matt |title=Omaha Blue Crew outlasts Team Overtime in a battle of old versus new |url=https://whiteandbluereview.com/omaha-blue-crew-outlasts-team-overtime-in-a-battle-of-old-versus-new/ |publisher=White and Blue Review |access-date=January 28, 2021 |date=July 17, 2022}} === City Reapers (2022–present) === In the 2022–23 OTE season, Thompson played for the City Reapers alongside team [[captain (sports)|captain]] Ausar, who selected him with the first pick in the league's draft.{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=OTE Announces Roster Reveal and Expansion for Season 2 |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/d8ad12ca-acbd-44d1-b6d9-9f5f1c5def45 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=September 21, 2022}} On January 9, 2023, he was named OTE Player of the Week, three days after recording 22 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists and five steals in a 101–90 win over the Cold Hearts.{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=Amen Thompson named OTE Player of the Week |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/83f18057-c9a9-4f28-b926-2592e600c537 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=January 9, 2023}} In the regular season, Thompson averaged 16.4 points, 5.9 rebounds, 5.9 assists and 2.3 steals per game and was named to the All-OTE First Team.{{Cite web |date=February 20, 2023 |title=OTE Announces Regular Season Awards |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/b66abb33-0079-4dc0-9858-7f6933f9a54a |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=OTE}}{{cite web |title=Amen Thompson |url=https://overtimeelite.com/players/e763b02b-3045-4a91-a078-7140899327d0/career |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 19, 2023}} In Game 2 of the OTE Finals, he made a game-winning layup at the buzzer in an 80–78 win over the YNG Dreamerz.{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=Amen Sinks Buzzer Beater for Reapers Game 2 Win |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/d021e545-7230-4b6d-af97-e01e51ee40f3 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 19, 2023 |date=March 4, 2023}} Thompson helped the Reapers win the league championship in a 3–0 [[Whitewash (sport)|sweep]].{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=City Reapers Win OTE Championship |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/81ad0922-4800-435b-9706-a5a6180ceb56 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 19, 2023 |date=March 4, 2023}} On April 21, 2023, he declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]], where analysts viewed him as a potential top-10 pick.{{cite web |last1=Cobb |first1=David |title=2023 NBA Draft: Amen, Ausar Thompson declare as likely lottery picks after playing for Overtime Elite |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2023-nba-draft-amen-ausar-thompson-declare-as-likely-lottery-picks-after-playing-for-overtime-elite/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]]
